title: Redis Caching
summary: Connect to Redis, choose keys and expiration, and read through a cache.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: How to Use Redis in Your Spring Boot Project: Step-by-Step Tutorial
Engineering Digest: How to integrate Redis Cloud with Spring Boot Application

richText: Use Redis as a cache
Redis stores values under keys. It can hold text and other data structures.
A cache stores a reusable copy of a value from a database or an external API.
A cache hit means the requested key has a value. A cache miss means no value is available.
On a miss, read the original source and store the result in the cache.
Time to live (TTL) is how long a key remains before Redis expires it.
Use a cache when repeated reads are expensive and briefly old data is acceptable. Keep important data in its original storage.
Connect Spring Boot to Redis
Add spring-boot-starter-data-redis. Boot configures Redis connections and templates from your settings.
Boot 3 uses spring.data.redis properties. Older examples may use spring.redis.
Your Redis provider supplies the host, port, username, and password.
TLS encrypts traffic between your application and Redis. Keep certificate validation enabled.

example.title: Configure a Redis Cloud connection
description: Add these settings to application.properties in a Spring Boot 3 application.
Set the REDIS_* environment variables from your provider’s connection details.
explanation: ssl.enabled enables TLS for the connection.
connect-timeout limits connection setup to two seconds.
timeout limits Redis operations to two seconds.

richText: Read and write cached values
StringRedisTemplate reads and writes string keys and string values.
ObjectMapper converts Java objects into JSON strings and back. Reuse the Boot-managed mapper.
Choose serialization explicitly. Declaring RedisTemplate does not by itself select JSON.
Include every input that changes the result in the key. For private data, include the user or tenant identity.

example.title: Cache weather for five minutes
description: Put this method in a service with injected StringRedisTemplate redis, ObjectMapper mapper, and WeatherProvider provider.
WeatherProvider.fetch(city) reads the original weather source.
Use Spring Boot 3, Spring Framework 6, and Java 17.
explanation: The key includes a normalized city name and a format version.
If Redis returns a string, the mapper reads it into Weather and the method returns it.
On a miss, the method calls the provider and rejects an empty result.
The fresh result is stored as JSON with a 300-second TTL.
Calls before expiration can reuse that result. Calls after expiration fetch a new result.
The method propagates Redis and JSON errors to its caller.

richText: Handle changes and failures
A TTL permits old values until the key expires. Delete or update the key after source changes when that delay is unacceptable.
A failed Redis connection is different from a cache miss.
For an optional cache, handle connection or decoding failures and fall back to the original source. Record the failure so it remains visible.
Two simultaneous misses can both call the original source. Add coordination when duplicate calls would exceed provider limits.
